draft.heroMessage: Paul Stevenson | Bend Oregon Real Estate
draft.welcomeNote: Welcome to transparent, attentive real estate in Bend and Central Oregon. I'm Paul Stevenson, a broker at Ryan Realty, and I'm here to make your home buying or selling experience as straightforward as possible.
draft.tagline: Local insight. Real answers. Every step of the way.
draft.aboutParagraph: As a broker at Ryan Realty, I work throughout Bend and across Central Oregon—helping buyers and sellers navigate the unique challenges and opportunities in our local markets. Whether you're searching for a first home, relocating, or looking for investment or resort properties, my focus is on providing honest, knowledgeable guidance and clear communication from your first question through closing. My goal is to match you with the neighborhood and the home that truly fits, with responsive service and an eye for detail that comes from living and working here every day.
draft.conciergeLine: Text or call me at 541-502-3436 for anything from a market update to a showing—you'll hear directly from me, not a call center.
draft.contactLine: Let's talk about your next move in Bend or Central Oregon. Reach out at paul@ryan-realty.com, or book a meeting when it works for you.
draft.tone: approachable, knowledgeable, and direct—focused on clear answers, local expertise, and personal communication.

sections.title: Selling questions
sections.body: Do I need to sign a listing agreement to get the CMA? No. The comparative market analysis is free, and there is no contract to sign to get it. If you read it and decide to list with us, that is a separate agreement we go through together. What does it cost to list with you? The listing fee is 3% of the sale price, with no add-on fees. That covers the MLS listing, professional photography, video, a 3D tour, the full marketing plan, every showing, and transaction management all the way through closing.

sections.title: What goes into the number
sections.body: Local comps Recent closed sales in your neighborhood and similar subdivisions set the floor and the ceiling. Active competition Days on market, sale-to-list ratios, and what is for sale near you now shape the list-price range. Your home Square footage, beds and baths, lot size, condition, and upgrades adjust the range for your property. How do I get my home's value in Bend? Use Value my home on this page.

sections.title: The team behind Ryan Realty
sections.body: How it started Matt Ryan, owner and principal broker, started Ryan Realty LLC in 2014 and opened the Bend office in June 2023, after years in the fire service. He learned the business from his mentor, Hjalmar "Red" Erickson, and runs the brokerage the way Red taught him: every client gets the same care and the same effort. The brokers Ryan Realty has three licensed brokers, and all three live and work in Central Oregon. Each broker's page has their Oregon license, recorded closings, and direct line.

sections.title: What different budgets tend to buy
sections.body: We do not print price bands here because they move every month. The pattern holds, though. At the entry level in Bend the choices are condos and townhomes, older homes on the east side, and smaller homes in the districts farther from downtown. The same money in Redmond buys a newer single-family home with a yard. Farther out, La Pine and Prineville buy more house again with a longer drive. The Bend and Redmond market pages show the current medians, and Bend vs Redmond vs Sisters covers the trade in each direction.

sections.title: What you are really choosing
sections.body: You are choosing between three things: how much house your money buys, how close you are to the things that made you look at Central Oregon, and how much town you want around you. Bend has the most of everything and costs the most. Redmond has the airport, a working downtown, and more house per dollar. Sisters is small, walkable, and quiet, with the Cascades right there. The live prices for each are on the market pages linked in each section.

sections.title: Loan program fees
sections.body: FHA. The upfront mortgage insurance premium is 1.75% of the base loan amount, and it can be financed into the loan. The annual premium on a 30-year loan with less than 5% down and a loan amount at or under the FHA base limit is 0.55% of the loan per year, collected monthly, per HUD's current mortgagee letter. VA. The funding fee for a purchase is 2.15% of the loan on first use with less than 5% down, 3.3% on later use, 1.5% with 5% or more down, and 1.25% with 10% or more down.

Selling questions
